title: Phone Home API Response Schema
description: Schema for the Phone Home API response (output of Report::getInfo() method)

constraint.description: The declared version constraint from package.json, with any user:password@ credentials stripped from URL constraints, or null if the value could not be processed

version.description: The version resolved from package-lock.json, with any user:password@ credentials stripped, or null when the lockfile is absent, is not parsed, or does not list the package

build_id.description: The unique build ID for currently deployed code

api_version.description: The version of the Phone Home API

timestamp.description: The timestamp when the report was generated

ip_address.description: The IP address of the server

composer_lock_updated.description: The timestamp when the composer.lock file was last updated, or null if it cannot be read

npm.description: Declared npm packages and their resolved versions. Always an object, so that a site with no npm dependencies can be told apart from a site whose dependencies could not be read; see status

status.description: The outcome of collecting this section. 'ok' means package.json was read and package-lock.json was read and parsed. 'no_manifest' means no package.json was found at any searched location, so the site genuinely has no npm dependencies. 'unreadable_manifest' means the manifest could not be read or parsed, either because a package.json is present but unreadable or because the project root could not be resolved. 'no_lockfile' means the manifest was read but no lockfile of any kind was found. 'unsupported_lockfile' means the manifest was read and a yarn.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml was found, which is named but not parsed. 'unreadable_lockfile' means the manifest was read but the lockfile could not be read or parsed

package_manager.description: The package manager detected by lockfile presence. This is null when no lockfile was found, and also when detection could not be completed, which a status of unreadable_lockfile indicates. Only npm lockfiles are parsed; yarn and pnpm are detected and named, but their declared packages report a null version

manifest_path.description: Where the package.json that was read lives, expressed relative to Craft's @root, for example '.' or '..'. Null when no manifest was found. Always relative, so no absolute server path is disclosed. This makes a misplaced manifest diagnosable from the report itself

lock_updated.description: The timestamp when the detected lockfile was last updated. This is null when no lockfile was found, and also when detection could not be completed. This is reported for yarn and pnpm lockfiles too, even though they are not parsed

dependencies.description: Declared production dependencies keyed by package name

dev_dependencies.description: Declared development dependencies keyed by package name

name.description: The name of the PHP interpreter

info.description: Detailed PHP information (only included if expandPhpInfo is true)

row_formats.description: InnoDB row-format census. Null when the question does not apply (PostgreSQL) or could not be answered, which must not be read as nothing being at risk.

at_risk.description: Tables in a row format subject to the 8126-byte row-size limit, which can block a future Craft migration

unknown.description: Tables whose row format could not be read; a census of these is not a census showing nothing at risk

tables.description: At-risk table names, bounded; at_risk carries the exact count

name.description: The image driver name (GD or Imagick)

total_available_updates.description: The total number of available updates

pending_migrations.description: The list of pending migration handles

was_craft_breakpoint_skipped.description: Whether a Craft breakpoint was skipped

is_craft_update_pending.description: Whether a Craft update is pending

is_plugin_update_pending.description: Whether a plugin update is pending

is_critical_update_available.description: Whether a critical update is available

additionalProperties.description: Additional system information (Yii, Twig, Guzzle versions if available)

is_upgrade_available.description: Whether an upgrade is available for the plugin

package_name.description: The plugin's Composer package name, e.g. verbb/formie. Null when Craft cannot attribute the plugin to a package

name.description: The name of the package with an available update

release_date.description: The release date of the update

status_checks.description: Results from registered status checks for monitoring application health

name.description: The human-readable name of the status check

status.description: The status level returned by the check

description.description: Optional description of what the check monitors

meta.description: Optional additional diagnostic information from the check

verification.description: Opt-in deployment-verification manifest. Absent on plugin versions that predate the contract, which a runner must treat as unsupported rather than as an empty passing suite.

schema_version.description: The manifest contract version the site is publishing

supported.description: Always true when the field is present; lets a runner distinguish an unsupported plugin from a disabled one

enabled.description: Whether the site has opted in by configuring any pages

valid.description: False when any definition failed validation, in which case pages is empty and errors explains why

pages.description: The pages to capture and assert. Empty whenever enabled or valid is false.

id.description: Stable identifier for this page, unique within the manifest

path.description: Site-relative path, resolved by the runner against an origin it is configured with separately

visible.description: Selector for an element that must be visible for the page to be considered correct

mask.description: Selectors whose text and pixels are excluded from comparison. Coverage deliberately given up, so it may never cover the asserted element.

errors.description: Human-readable validation failures. Non-empty only when valid is false.

verification_coverage.description: How much of what the site renders the manifest watches. Null when it could not be answered, which must not be read as full coverage. Counting pages is close to meaningless; templates are the measure that predicts whether a break would be caught.

scope.description: Element types counted in the denominator; anything outside this renders through templates nobody is measuring

templates_total.description: Distinct templates that render a routable URL

templates_covered.description: Of those, how many at least one manifest page renders through

uncovered.description: Templates no manifest page exercises, bounded; the counts stay exact

routable_uris.description: Routable URLs in scope, context for the template numbers rather than a coverage measure itself

unmatched_paths.description: Manifest paths that resolve to no element in scope, such as a custom route; they cannot be credited as covering a template
